The Temptations - (I Know) I'm Losing You (1966)

"(I Know) I'm Losing You" is a 1966 hit single recorded by The Temptations for the Gordy (Motown) label and produced by Norman Whitfield. Lead vocals were by David Ruffin and background vocals by Eddie Kendricks, Paul Williams, Melvin Franklin and Otis Williams. The guitar work was by Cornelius Grant backed by The Funk Brothers, who were a group of Detroit-based session musicians who performed the backing to most Motown recordings from 1959 until the company moved to Los Angeles in 1972.

They are considered one of the most successful groups of studio musicians in music history, alongside the Wrecking Crew. The Funk Brothers played on Motown hits such as "My Girl", "I Heard It Through the Grapevine", "Baby Love", "Signed, Sealed, Delivered I'm Yours", "Papa Was a Rollin' Stone", "The Tears of a Clown", "Ain't No Mountain High Enough", and "Heat Wave".

A successful, longer cover version was released by Rare Earth in 1970. Rare Earth's 10-minute cover was edited for single release and peaked at No. 7, one position higher than the Temptations' original on the U.S. pop charts.
